subject: Clarifying service-provider scope, subprocessors, and cross-state transfer evidence
messages:

Subject: RFI: service provider scope + subprocessors for CPRA/CA use case

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for taking this on. As we prepare intake for our privacy team, a couple of targeted asks so we can map Redwood into our CPRA Annex: 

1) Can you confirm Redwood's legal role under CPRA/CPRA (i.e., "service provider" / processor) for hosted API usage and whether that characterization holds for Dedicated capacity?
2) We need a current list of subprocessors (vendor name, country, purpose, access type) and any planned onshore fallback options if offshoring is restricted.
3) For transfers across state lines and offshore backups, what technical/contractual controls are in place (e.g., encryption in transit & at rest, access controls, subprocessor agreements)?
4) Please share evidence artifacts you can provide: SOC 2 (most recent), subprocessor attestation, DPA redline (preferred) and an estimated timeline to get a signed DPA.

I've attached our short RFI and DPA draft for reference. Would appreciate a response by EOD Friday so we can brief internal counsel.

Regards,

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: RFI: service provider scope + subprocessors for CPRA/CA use case

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, attaching our up-to-date subprocessor inventory and SOC 2 cover page. Full SOC 2 report can be shared under NDA / secure link.

Short answers:
- Role: For hosted API and Redwood Dedicated (customer-owned pool) we are a "service provider" / processor under CPRA language when customers send personal data to our hosted inference runtime. For Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) customers control the environment and data flows — in those cases Redwood acts more as a software vendor/processor depending on the deployment model. We'll commit to the service-provider role in the DPA for hosted & dedicated modes used by HealthOps.

- Subprocessors: see attached CSV (redwood_subprocessors_nov2026.csv). Key notes:
  * Core inference runtime (GPU infra) operated by Redwood in our cloud regions (US, EU).
  * Managed telemetry & analytics (aggregated performance metrics) is routed to a separate telemetry service — telemetry access is limited, and telemetry data is pseudonymized for unit economics.
  * A small set of managed support contractors in India and Canada have limited access for incident triage under MFA and time-limited privileged sessions.

- Transfers & controls: encryption in transit (TLS1.3) and at rest (AES-256). Role-based access controls, logging, and just-in-time privileged access. We execute subprocessor agreements with the same processor/service-provider commitments. For customers requiring onshore-only processing we offer Dedicated onshore pools and Private (VPC/on-prem) options.

- Evidence & timeline: We can provide: SOC 2 Type II (Q3 2026), subprocessor inventory export, and a DPA redline. If HealthOps can send a final DPA draft by Friday we can aim for a redline within 3 business days and a signed DPA within 10 business days pending legal review.

Next steps I suggest:
1) HealthOps confirms deployment mode(s) (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).
2) We provide a DPA redline + SOC2 secure link.
3) Schedule a short call (30 min) to walk legal through our subprocessors and onshore fallback options.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Subject: Internal: suggested DPA redline points for HealthOps

Tessa — filing a short note to capture legal asks we should proactively include in our redline to avoid back-and-forth: 

1) Explicit "service provider" designation for hosted & dedicated (call out Dedicated as processor for the reserved pool usage).
2) No-sale/limited-use clause: clarify telemetry/usage metrics are aggregated and not "sale" under CPRA; add explicit prohibition on using personal data for model training or advertising.
3) Subprocessor updates: provide 30-day notice of material additions and offer onshore fallback plan for critical subprocessors.
4) Data subject rights: outline support process and SLA for deletion/erasure requests coming through HealthOps (we'll surface logs and support, but customer manages identity proofing).
5) Incident response & audit: SOC2 report provision, 3rd-party audit evidence, and SOC log extracts on request under NDA.
6) Limitations: telemetry pseudonymization exception — call this out in the DPA as an operational carve-out with strict access controls.

Marissa — can you confirm the short notice timeline for subprocessor onboarding (30 days) and whether we can commit to a secure SOC 2 link instead of sending full PDFs by default?

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
